ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, particularly Chapter 11 on Yuhan Hoesa and Article 317 on registration; Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, particularly Articles 2, 5-2 and 5-3; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 5 and 6; Real Name Financial Transactions and Privacy Act, Article 3; Supreme Court Registration of Commerce Rules; Financial Services Commission Guidelines on Customer Due Diligence; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registration Office (Commercial Registration Division)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For destination states party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille solely from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For destination states not party to the Convention, obtain Consular Legalization solely from the Korean Embassy or Consulate with consular jurisdiction. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Equivalent: Certificate of Current Corporate Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registration Office and/or National Tax Service, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the official certificate from the issuing registry or tax office; if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, authenticate solely by attaching an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If the receiving jurisdiction is a non-member state, authenticate solely via Consular Legalization by the destination state's Korean embassy or consulate; Apostille and Consular Legalization are alternative routes and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution Authorizing Incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, authenticated by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The directors' signatures and corporate seal must be notarized by a Korean notary public. For an Apostille Convention destination, the notarized instrument is then authenticated solely by an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For a non-Convention destination, the notarized instrument is authenticated solely through Consular Legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission of that destination. Never apply both authentication paths sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders of Yuhan Hoesa and Korean notarial office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The Articles must be executed before and notarized by a Korean notary public. If the destination state is a Hague Apostille Convention member, attach an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If the destination state is not an Apostille member, proceed exclusively by Consular Legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel, mutually exclusive, and may not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea maintaining the proposed corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be issued on official letterhead and the authorizing bank officer's signature and corporate seal must be notarized. For an Apostille Convention state, authenticate by Apostille from the Republic of Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-member state, authenticate exclusively by Consular Legalization before the Korean embassy or consulate with jurisdiction. Apostille and Consular Legalization remain mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding, counsel must screen every shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, and authorized signatory against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and Financial Supervisory Service PEP and sanction alerts; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; Korean designated persons under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Regulation of International Financial Transactions; and adverse media databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory if any UBO is a foreign PEP, holds 25 percent or more, or uses any nominee, proxy, layered, or trust arrangement. The ongoing CDD file must include a valid passport, certified corporate registry extract, tax residence certificate, source of funds narrative, and a negative sanctions hit report. Re-screening is required every 180 days and immediately before any capital disbursement, equity transfer, or change of directors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Online Registration System (I-Ros Internet Registration Office) and National Tax Service Business Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be formed in Hangul using the Korean corporate form designation Yuhan Hoesa. A foreign or Western trade name may appear as a transliterated Hangul alias, but the Hangul name remains the controlling registered name. Four-tier naming conventions apply: Tier 1, an identical existing Hangul name in the same registration district must be rejected; Tier 2, a confusingly similar name of an existing legal entity with the same principal business object must be rejected or revised; Tier 3, transliterated foreign names may be accepted when the Hangul spelling is distinct and the business code differs; Tier 4, names containing restricted or sensitive tokens require the relevant ministry or regulator approval prior to registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a full or partial name rejection, the applicant must obtain the written rejection notice citing the conflicting registration, the similarity standard, or the restricted token. Within 14 days of receipt, the applicant must file a formal administrative objection with the competent Supreme Court Registration Office and a parallel appeal with the Seoul Administrative Court or the relevant district court, attaching the proposed name, the business scope certificate, evidence of distinctiveness, and any ministerial approvals. If the rejection is based on phonetic similarity, the applicant may present an alternative multi-word Hangul name and seek a priority re-examination within 7 business days. The registry is required to issue a reasoned written disposition, and judicial review may be requested if the objection remains unresolved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may be accepted by the court registry for initial incorporation only where a licensed registered agent or law firm provides a physical address and mail forwarding arrangement. However, the National Tax Service, local district offices, and Korean banks generally reject a pure virtual office for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in IoT hardware retail because physical presence, inventory records, administrative capacity, and VAT invoice issuance must be verifiable. Stripe and Shopify Payments integrations also require a verified business location and are likely to reject a mailbox-only address under AML and real-name verification rules. A serviced office lease with dedicated suite access and evidence of occupancy is the minimum acceptable commercial substance; full virtual-office reliance is not reliably permissible for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection by the National Tax Service, municipal authorities, or registry officials: (1) conspicuous display of the business registration certificate; (2) physical signage matching the registered name; (3) lease agreement and utility bills in the company name; (4) board minutes designating the registered office; (5) actual personnel, attendance records, and corporate books; (6) inventory and shipping records for IoT hardware; (7) VAT invoices, receipts, and bank statements; and (8) board resolution authorizing the business premise. Quantified risk for the first tax year is elevated at approximately 45-60 percent for retail e-commerce and IoT hardware businesses due to VAT verification and consumer protection inspections; after a clean filing record, probability reduces to 15-25 percent per subsequent year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), specifically Articles 543-620 (Limited Liability Company) and Article 289 (incorporation procedures).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division, Korean District Court of the principal place of business (e.g., Seoul Central District Court).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Certificate of Incorporation (등기사항증명서).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korea does not impose a minimum capital requirement for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the capital must be fully paid up at incorporation and the amount must be stated in the Articles of Incorporation. No escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE INITIAL DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA)

The undersigned, being the initial directors of [Company Name] (the 'Company'), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, hereby adopt the following resolutions in accordance with the Company's Articles of Incorporation and the Commercial Act of South Korea:

1. Share Capital Subscription: The Company's total issued share capital is set at KRW [amount] (the 'Total Capital'), divided into [number] shares of no par value. Each director hereby acknowledges that the Total Capital has been fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The directors confirm that the capital is held in the Company's designated bank account and shall be used solely for the Company's legitimate business purposes.

2. Banking Authorization: The directors authorize the opening of a corporate bank account with [Bank Name] and designate the following individuals as authorized signatories: [Name], [Name], and [Name]. Any two of the authorized signatories shall jointly execute all banking transactions, including but not limited to deposits, withdrawals, wire transfers, and issuance of checks, subject to the Company's internal control policies and applicable banking regulations.

3. Registered Office Adoption: The registered office of the Company shall be established at [Address], which is within the jurisdiction of the [Court Name] District Court. The directors confirm that the registered office is a permanent physical location where legal documents and official correspondence may be served, and that the Company's statutory records, including the register of members and minutes, will be maintained at this address.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments: The following officers are appointed to serve in the capacities indicated: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall have the authority and responsibilities as defined in the Company's Articles of Incorporation and applicable law. The officers shall serve until their successors are duly elected and qualified, and they are authorized to execute all documents and take all actions necessary for the Company's operations.

5. General Provisions: The directors and officers are hereby authorized to take all necessary steps, execute all necessary documents, and make all filings required to effectuate the incorporation of the Company, including but not limited to registration with the competent Korean court, obtaining business registration certificates from the National Tax Service, and ensuring compliance with all applicable tax, licensing, and regulatory requirements.

This resolution is effective as of the date of adoption and shall be recorded in the Company's minute book.

Adopted this [day] of [month], [year], by the undersigned initial directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (공증인) and the Korean District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, business purpose, total capital, number of shares, and initial directors. Ensure all founders sign the document. Submit the draft to a Korean notary for notarization, which verifies the authenticity of signatures and the legal capacity of the founders. After notarization, prepare the incorporation application form and all supporting documents for submission to the court. The notarization process is mandatory for the validity of the Articles and must be completed before any registration filing.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all founders (passport or Korean ID)
Power of attorney if any founder is represented
Consent forms from initial directors accepting their appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the Articles due to errors or omissions, correct the identified issues and resubmit. If the court later queries the notarization, provide additional clarifications or re-notarize as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank in South Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the company's name at a Korean commercial bank. Deposit the full amount of the stated capital into this account. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (예금증명서) confirming the capital payment. This certificate is a mandatory document for the court registration. Ensure the bank account is opened in the exact company name as per the Articles of Incorporation. The deposit must be made before the court filing, and the certificate must be dated within a few days of submission.
required_dossiers: Identification of the person opening the account (director or authorized agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing documents or correct the company name. If the certificate is delayed, request an expedited issuance or obtain a provisional certificate from the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, Korean District Court (e.g., Seoul Central District Court)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application to the competent court. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of capital deposit, the consent forms of directors, and the completed registration form (상업등기신청서). Pay the registration fee (approximately KRW 150,000) at the court's revenue office. The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court issues a Certificate of Incorporation (등기사항증명서), which legally establishes the company. The entire process typically takes 5 business days.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query or suspension, respond within 2 weeks with the requested clarifications or additional documents. Common issues include discrepancies in the company name or capital amount; correct these and resubmit. If the application is rejected, appeal or re-file after rectifying the defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) Local District Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, register the company for business with the NTS to obtain a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증). This registration is mandatory for tax purposes and to open a permanent corporate bank account. Submit the application form (사업자등록신청서) along with the Certificate of Incorporation, the company's corporate seal certificate, and the director's identification. The NTS will issue the certificate within 3 business days. This certificate is also required for obtaining any industry-specific licenses, though none are mandated for retail IoT hardware sales.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the application due to incomplete information, correct the form and resubmit. If the office requests additional documentation, provide it promptly. In case of delays, contact the NTS hotline or visit the office in person to expedite.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, acting through the Home Tax Service (HTS) online electronic portal located at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that engages in or owns a Korean business entity must ensure that the Korean domestic entity, including a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company, files for a Business Registration Number with the local district tax office or through the Home Tax Service within 20 days after business commencement. For a foreign entity that itself carries on trade or business through a permanent establishment in Korea, an ex officio registration as a foreign corporation is required through the competent tax office, accompanied by the designation of a domestic tax representative, the articles of incorporation, certificate of foreign registration or equivalent authentication, power of attorney, and proof of appointment of the representative. The Business Registration Number issued by the NTS serves as the unified corporate tax identification number and the Value Added Tax registration number for indirect tax purposes. For foreign non-resident entities without a Korean place of business, no Korean TIN is obtained unless the entity is required to file Korean income tax or VAT in respect of domestic supplies; in such cases, a withholding agent or domestic tax representative must complete the relevant registration via HTS before any tax filing obligation arises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under any US-style check-the-box election; a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation taxed at the entity level on its worldwide income. No hybrid mismatch elections are available. A statutory group tax consolidation election may be applied by a domestic controlling parent over its wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries subject to approval under Article 50 of the Corporate Tax Act, but this does not alter the entity-level classification of the LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold; every person who independently supplies goods or services in the course of business, whether resident or non-resident, must register for VAT with the National Tax Service. A Simplified Taxpayer regime may apply to small businesses with annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000, but VAT registration remains mandatory and the simplified regime does not exempt the taxpayer from reporting obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses are mandated to issue electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) for supplies to other businesses through the Home Tax Service (HTS). The issuance details, including supply value and calculated VAT, must be transmitted electronically to the NTS in real time or no later than the next business day using HTS API integration or the HTS web platform. Each e-invoice contains a mandatory transaction-specific invoice number and a generated electronic verification code; there is no separate physical fiscal stamp. A penalty of up to 2% of the supply value for non-issuance or late issuance of the e-invoice applies, and failure to submit correct data may trigger further administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Korea qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 21 of the Value Added Tax Act where the goods leave the territory of Korea pursuant to an approved customs export declaration and the exporter holds evidence of the completed exportation. Services supplied to non-residents, including qualifying offshore digital services and certain ancillary services for exported goods, are zero-rated when the consideration is paid in foreign currency from abroad, the services are consumed or used outside Korea, and the exporter retains documentary evidence of the foreign performance. Supplies of goods to a non-resident inside Korea destined for export may be conditionally zero-rated when the goods are entered into a bonded area and subsequently exported within the statutorily prescribed period. The exporter must maintain, at the place of business, all records sufficient to prove the physical export, the foreign recipient, and the eventual receipt of consideration from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration and electronic clearance receipt issued or lodged through Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (Ocean Waybill) or Air Waybill as the authoritative shipping contract
Electronic Tax Invoice (e-invoice) marked or annotated as zero-rated export supply
Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, serving as the Korean equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
Export Performance Certificate or equivalent NTS-relevant evidence when requested by the tax office to substantiate the actual export, value, and payment flow
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may audit zero-rated export transactions for up to 10 years where fraud is suspected and may claw back input VAT credits and impose VAT at the standard 10% rate on the supply if the exporter fails to substantiate exportation or if the overseas consideration is not repatriated within the statutory deadline. Administrative penalties include a 40% additional tax on the amount of input tax incorrectly claimed, understatement penalties of 10% to 30% of the tax understated, and late-payment interest overdue daily. For intentional evasion involving forged customs declarations or counterfeit foreign exchange certificates, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act allows criminal prosecution, imprisonment up to three years, and fines. Additionally, the Korea Customs Service may impose independent penalties for false declaration or customs document fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an open-market regime with the current account fully convertible and the capital account subject to registration or reporting. For an IoT hardware retail Yuhan Hoesa, import payments for inventory, software licensing, and platform service fees are current account transactions and are freely permitted after the submission of standard supporting documents to a licensed foreign exchange bank of the entity's choice. Equity injections by non-resident shareholders are capital account transactions that require advance FDI registration under Article 23 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA); once registered, conversion into KRW is automatic, and no individual central bank approval is needed. Profit remittances via shareholder dividends require tax clearance and the submission of a foreign exchange purchase confirmation to the settlement bank; the key limitation is the documentary burden, not permission. Korea does not impose export proceeds surrender quotas; however, all export receipts must be either retained in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or converted to KRW within a statutory settlement period of 15 months from the export declaration date, and each conversion must be reported to the settlement bank in the Electronic Foreign Exchange Information System. Treasury liquidity is therefore highly mobile for bona fide trade flows, while regulatory scrutiny is concentrated on UBO transparency, trade substance, and proper tax clearance before capital account transactions such as dividend remittances are completed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 33(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export receipts must be collected within 15 months from the date of export declaration, with extensions up to 6 years available for capital goods or defense-related transactions. The collected foreign currency proceeds may be deposited into a Foreign Currency Account at a domestic DMB; the mandatory conversion ratio into KRW is 0%, meaning full retention in foreign currency is permitted. However, any optional conversion to KRW must be executed at a licensed foreign exchange bank and submitted through the bank's e-reporting system under the proper trade-related foreign exchange purpose code. Balances held in the FCA are subject to quarterly reporting to the Bank of Korea through the designated bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Currency Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Offshore digital EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, and flexible fintech treasury platforms are legally barred from serving as the primary corporate bank or FX settlement rail for a Korean-resident legal entity. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only a domestic licensed financial institution with a Foreign Exchange Business Registration can perform foreign exchange deposit, conversion, and payment execution for a Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa. Stripe and Shopify Payments may be used only as merchant acquiring channels for domestic e-commerce card transactions; the settlement of a Korean entity's cross-border consumer receipts must occur into a KRW merchant account at a licensed domestic bank, which then performs the conversion. Any direct USD or other foreign-currency treasury balance held offshore through an EMI would constitute an unregistered foreign exchange entity exposure and expose the company to criminal fines and sanctions. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must rest entirely on domestic Tier-1 banks, with EMI rails limited to terminal merchant acquiring.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of a statutory director or a locally appointed representative with power of attorney is mandatory at a Korean domestic bank branch for the initial corporate KYC interview and account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally acceptable for a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa without any prior banking relationship; the bank requires a face-to-face identification under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the AML/CFT obligations of the Financial Action Task Force. A non-resident director may make a single trip to Seoul to complete the interview, or the company must register a local resident representative director with the Korean court registry, which creates shared control risk. For capitals, there is no exception for fully digital onboarding. The supporting identification documents must be apostilled or consular-legalized, and all powers of attorney must be notarized and translated into Korean by a registered translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder with 100% ownership injecting initial capital from a jurisdiction with weak corporate substance (e.g., a BVI or Seychelles holding company).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A UBO diagram showing every intermediate entity through to natural persons, apostilled certificates of incorporation of the parent entity, audited financial statements of the parent for the last two years, certified passport copies of the ultimate shareholders, source-of-funds declaration, a bank reference letter from the sending bank, and a notarized letter confirming the economic substance of the parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, geographically dispersed consumer card settlement from Stripe and Shopify Payments without a clearly identifiable physical retail operation in Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant service agreements with Stripe and Shopify Payments, 12 months of settlement and chargeback statements, transaction-level exports from the e-commerce platforms, CRM order logs showing customer destinations and IP addresses, a physical warehouse or third-party logistics contract in Korea, and a compliant VAT issuance history proving bona fide retail sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, rapid outbound payments to multiple overseas IoT hardware manufacturers in short succession, creating an unusual payment structuring pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders and supplier pro-forma invoices, B/L (Bill of Lading) or air waybill evidence, customs import declarations in Korea, pre-shipment inspection certificates, delivery terms (Incoterms) in the trade contracts, a written rationale for splitting payments, and the Yuhan Hoesa board resolution authorizing the disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate withdrawal of three-quarters of the registered capital from the escrow account to pay for imported hardware inventory before any realized consumer revenue has been recorded.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed working capital schedule and inventory purchase forecast, supplier inventory allocation agreements, a pro-forma invoice with a clear production timeline, a duty and import tax assessment from the Korean Customs Service, and a board resolution certifying that the capital drawdown is strictly for the registered business scope of smart IoT device retailing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All non-resident equity injections into the Yuhan Hoesa must first be registered as Foreign Direct Investment with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Bank of Korea through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The overseas investor should instruct its remitting bank to send a SWIFT MT103, using the cross-border purpose code for foreign direct investment capital contribution (typically classification code 701500 in the Korean foreign exchange information system), addressed to the Yuhan Hoesa's Capital Escrow Account at a Tier-1 Korean bank. Upon receipt, the Korean bank generates a Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate, and after a statutory registration filing with the 'Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency' or delegated Korean bank, the funds are eligible for transfer into the operational KRW account. Capital verification is then completed by an independent Korean certified public accountant, who reviews the foreign currency deposit certificate, the FDI registration certificate, the bank incoming wire confirmation, and the shareholder resolution; a Capital Verification Report is issued and filed with the National Tax Service. Shareholder loans must be separately registered under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot be commingled with share capital; each loan inflow requires a separate loan registration with a purpose code and drawee-confirmation through the same domestic bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Direct supplier payment for IoT hardware inventory should be made in USD or CNY via SWIFT MT103 from the Yuhan Hoesa's foreign currency account at the Korean settlement bank, with the underlying trade invoice, packing list, and commercial contract attached to the forex remittance application. For large-value shipments above USD 200,000, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) opened through a Korean bank and advised through the supplier's confirming bank is the recommended clearing rail, as it preserves documentary control over the goods. Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) may be used for low-risk recurring suppliers with a proven delivery track record; the presenting bank will release documents against payment or acceptance, supported by the supplier's presentation of ocean/international transport documents. All outbound disbursements must be mapped to active purchase orders in the entity's ERP, and any FX remittance above an internal threshold of USD 80,000 triggers an automatic bank compliance review requiring the full trade file in Korean or English. Domestic KRW disbursements to Korean logistics vendors and warehousing providers are cleared through the Korean Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute (KFTC) interbank rails, not through cross-border SWIFT, and should be made from the operational KRW account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (Tom-Next, 1M to 12M) with a licensed Korean bank, underpinned by a confirmed inbound sales or outbound inventory-purchase invoice as the required underlying trade exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for crossing KRW against USD or CNY where the entity needs to hedge a non-commercial offshore treasury exposure, with the Korean bank acting as the counterparty and requiring an underlying balance-sheet exposure certificate
Cross-currency swaps for long-term foreign-currency vendor debt denominated in USD or Chinese Yuan, limited to the principal and interest profile of the actual outstanding external borrowing

Foreign currency plain-vanilla call and put options for managing the volatility of future Amazon/e-commerce settlement receipts, subject to the daily position limit of 125% of the projected trade inflow for the next 90 days

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments.permissible_instrument_boundary: All hedging instruments must be evidence-based and used for de-risking actual trade exposure; speculative naked FX transactions are prohibited and would void the bank's license protection under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments for IoT inventory should be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the Yuhan Hoesa's foreign currency account at the domestic Korean bank, coded correctly under the Foreign Exchange Information System (e.g., purpose code for trade settlement). For larger recurring shipments, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) is preferred, issued by KB Kookmin, Shinhan, or Woori Bank and advised through the overseas supplier's bank, with the payment released against compliant documents (invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin). Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are permissible for low-risk or stable vendors where the bank acts as a collecting agent; the Korean bank will require the seller's draft and transport documents. Each disbursement above USD 100,000 will trigger an automatic AML trade-screening check; the treasury must attach a purchase order, pro-forma invoice, customs declaration history, and evidence of the escrow account balance as part of the underlying transaction defense.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, by 31 March of the following year, extendable to 31 May when the corporate tax return is prepared and adjusted by a certified tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax under Article 66 of the Corporate Income Tax Act; negligent understatement penalty of 10%; daily overdue interest charged from the original due date; NTS may issue estimated assessment and enforce collection through attachment and public auction of assets. Administrative strike-off is not directly available to the NTS for private corporations, but continued delinquency exposes the entity to tax liens and compulsory collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local revenue administration (si/gun/gu) through the Integrated Local Tax Information System at the principal place of tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the corporate income tax return deadline; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa filing by 31 March, local corporate income tax is due by 30 April; if the extended 31 May national return is used, the local return is due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty under the Local Tax Act of 20% of the local income tax due; understated tax penalty of 10%; daily overdue interest from the statutory due date; persistent non-payment subjects bank accounts and receivables to local-government seizure and public auction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Returns for the two semi-annual VAT taxable periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Interim return for January-March on 25 April; final return for January-June on 25 July; interim return for July-September on 25 October; final return for July-December on 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid VAT; unfaithful-return penalty on overstated input tax credits; daily overdue interest; repeated delinquency triggers compulsory collection, seizure of assets, and closure of the business place by the competent NTS district office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll Withholding Year-End Reconciliation and Wage/Payment Certificate Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer submission of annual wage/payment statements and year-end withholding reconciliation data by 28 February following the tax year, or by 10 March when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-submission penalty of 1% of the unreported wage/payment amount; failure to submit withholding certificates can result in additional withholding assessments, penalty surcharges, and, if done willfully, criminal liability under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing and Certified Financial Statements (mandatory only for an audited Yuhan Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor's report must be issued and filed with the FSS/SFC before or at the annual members' meeting approving the financial statements; for a calendar-year audited Yuhan Hoesa, the ordinary members' meeting and filing milestone generally occur by 31 March, with the audit report filed within 2 weeks thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the audit report is a regulatory violation under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; subject to corrective orders, audit-designation sanctions, administrative fines, and in serious cases criminal penalties against directors; tax authorities may disregard unaudited financial statements for assessment purposes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National CIT 9% on the first KRW 200 million, 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 25% on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion; plus a 10% local income tax surcharge (aggregate equivalent 9.9% / 20.9% / 27.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general patent box regime; available incentives include special R&D tax credits under the Tax Incentives Limitation Act, foreign-investment free-zone corporate tax reductions (typically 50-100% temporary exemptions for qualifying high-tech/new-growth industries), SME income and education tax reductions, and investment tax credits for automation/energy-saving facilities; all incentives require documentary economic substance in Korea.
